definitions.explanation: In karate and several other martial arts, paired training or competition in which two practitioners exchange techniques. Contrasted with solo {型|かた} (forms) practice.

examples.japanese: {組|く}み{手|て}の{練習|れんしゅう}をする。
{彼|かれ}は{組|く}み{手|て}が{得意|とくい}だ。
{空手|からて}の{試合|しあい}は{型|かた}と{組|く}み{手|て}の{二|ふた}つの{部門|ぶもん}に{分|わ}かれている。
examples.english: Karate competitions are divided into two divisions: forms and sparring.

notes:
From {組|く}む (to join, to engage) + {手|て} (hand). The image is two opponents 'joining hands' — engaging each other in technique exchange.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {組|く}み{手|て}{試合|じあい}: a sparring match
- {自由|じゆう}{組|く}み{手|て}: free sparring (unscripted)
- {約束|やくそく}{組|く}み{手|て}: prearranged sparring (set sequence)

USAGE:
Most strongly associated with karate, where competition is split into {型|かた} (kata, solo forms) and {組|く}み{手|て} (kumite, sparring). Also used in {柔道|じゅうどう}, {合気道|あいきどう}, and other arts. Both 'kata' and 'kumite' are used as loanwords in English-speaking martial arts communities.
